title: DeJitter admission fence and kernel-probe matrix for continuous batching
creator: Priya Patel
description: Summary: We observe persistent 95th/99th token-latency regressions under mixed-tenancy continuous workloads when the kernel selection logic attempts aggressive coalescing. This ticket implements a DeJitter Admission Fence (per-tenant time-dejitter buckets + controlled admission windows) paired with a Kernel-Probe Matrix (systematic probing to build a live latency/throughput profile per model-variant/hardware kernel). The admission fence smooths burst arrivals to avoid creating pathological batch shapes; the probe matrix drives low-overhead kernel-selection decisions and fallback triggers for quantized or small-sequence kernels. Goal: reduce 95th/99th tail by at least 15% without increasing mean latency by more than 5% and keep cost/unit stable.
acceptance_criteria: 95th token latency reduction >= 15% on mixed-tenancy replay workloads (stable within 3 independent runs)
Mean token latency increase <= 5% measured on the nightly benchmark harness (same dataset)
No customer-facing error-rate increase; system-level dropped-request rate < 0.01% during canary
Probe telemetry available in Console per-model (latency histogram, probe-count, preferred-kernel) and dashboard showing kernel-switch events
Feature flag gated rollout with canary on 5% of instances and automatic rollback on SLO breach
notes: 2026-02-25 - Kickoff: scoped DeJitter admission fence + kernel-probe matrix. Initial design doc linked. Priya wrote prototype admission window algorithm.

2026-03-01 - Experiment v1: simulated 10k RPS mixed-tenancy trace. DeJitter reduced 99th by ~18% but increased mean by ~8% in worst-case (small sequences). Decision: add per-tenant jitter-bucket sizing and 'fast-path' for <=8-token requests.

2026-03-04 - Design review with Runtime team. Feedback: ensure probe sampling rate is bounded to avoid overhead; prefer lightweight in-kernel counters. Agreed to sample 0.5% of prefills per minute per model by default and exponential backoff when stable.

2026-03-06 - Security review: no customer data stored, only anonymized latency histograms. Security flagged KMS gating for telemetry export; follow-up ticket if exporting to external analytics (deferred).

2026-03-09 - Implementation: admission fence implemented as a per-GPU in-memory ring of time-buckets with token credit smoothing. Kernel-probe matrix implemented as a side-table keyed by (model-id, kernel-variant, seq-length-bin, gpu-family). Probe sampler emits metrics to statsd and Console via new metric names: kernel_probe.latency_ms, admission.dejitter_delay_ms, admission.rejected_count.

2026-03-11 - Bench results on staging: mixed-tenancy replay: 95th down 16.2%, 99th down 14.8%. Mean up 3.1%. CPU overhead measured +1.7% on control-plane. Memory increase ~0.3% per worker. Tuning: reduced per-tenant bucket depth to shave memory; introduced fast-path for tiny requests to avoid added jitter.

2026-03-12 - Pre-canary checklist complete. Added kill-switch flag and observability dashboards. Plan: canary 5% runtime fleet for 48h, evaluate SLOs and kernel-switch churn. If stable, escalate to 25% then full rollout.

Trade-offs: DeJitter reduces tail but introduces small artificial queuing delay; mitigations include size-based fast-path, tenant-priority bypass, and adaptive bucket sizing. Kernel-probe sampling adds noise but critical for adaptive kernel selection under nonstationary workloads.
Open questions: how to reconcile probe results across Dedicated vs Hosted hardware (we currently keep separate matrices but consider cross-pollination for models with limited samples).
deployment_plan: feature-flagged: runtime.feature.dejitter=true. Canary path: 5% instances (48h) -> 25% (72h) -> 100% (rollout). Automatic rollback if 95th token latency increases >5% or error-rate >0.02%.
rollback_plan: Immediate flag flip to false. Move canary traffic back to stable scheduler. Postmortem required if rollback occurs: include timeline, kernel-switch events, probe counts, and customer impact.
owner_notes: Daniel to own runtime changes; Priya to own telemetry/console work. Follow-on tickets expected for: (a) cross-pollination of probe matrix across Dedicated clusters, (b) UI filters to inspect per-tenant dejitter windows.
